touches.text: Each depositor gets its own index over the shared nodes, because each asked different questions first while assimilating the data.

The shape: one long list of nodes, id = row. Each tree has its own table and asks one question. Weights are in the leaves. Links are bidirectional. A tree past 5K leaves is calved at its dominant attractors, a deterministic code shear. Different trees can index the same data in different ways. (Akien 2026-11-03)

The librarian owns every tree and delegates ownership of some to the devices that learn: CodeMother, chart, any learning block holds its own trees by the librarian's delegation (Law 6: delegation through the owner's gate). Why: two holders with different weights over the same nodes have different perspectives and can debate points, and the librarian, asked anything, can look at the query from both. (Akien 2026-11-05)

Delegation nests down the rungs: the librarian delegates a set of trees to a device, the device to its machines, a machine to its tools if one is ever that complex. Each stays co-owned by the one above. CodeMother's learning goes in its own tables, and she owns the learning blocks of her machines and tools. (Akien 2026-11-05)
Each device growing its own pool of tables (today: 16 node tables, several owners).
Walks go through the librarian's published trees tool, not the bus (2.2.8.1.2).

Most devices submit queries to the trees and never walk them: walk, nearest and neighbors are encapsulated by the librarian, which owns the processes of memory the way CodeMother owns the code and sees to its well-being (10.1). They can be made available through a tree class and bus verbs, but using memory happens at a higher level than that for most devices. (Q#29, Akien 2026-11-05: "that's why we have the librarian at all, to encapsulate and own those processes")

Prebuild face: the chart chain, eight machines, each answering one question before a build begins: orient (what is asked, where does it live), constrain (what bounds it), survey (what already exists), decompose (how does it split), triage (what first, by what standard), hypothesize (what do we expect, how would we know we're wrong), validate (what does DONE mean, measured), and after the build, verdict (what done actually meant).

Owns the inspectors and gates (draft, moving from standalone): build_inspector, plan_inspector, ticket_inspector, corrosion, exemptions, rehearsal, determinism, import_sieve, and the tester (11; Q#33, Akien 2026-10-29). (Not diagnostic_inspector: it is base's, 17.3.) The code pipeline's inspectors and gates move to CodeMother; any that are not about code (if such existed) would not. (Q#31, Akien 2026-10-27)
Publishes a client tool (connect, read, write, query ...) that talks to the database over its socket, no bus hop: faster (2.2.8.1.1).

tree: the nexus graph-tree face (deposit, counsel, propose) over the librarian's trees. It is the same tool everywhere, not chart's: it is written as chart's only because chart was where it was first defined at that level. It stays a tool and does not fold into the librarian's verbs; a learning block holding its trees by the librarian's delegation (4.3.1.6) works them through it. A learning block that needs a special adaptation gets a subclass. (Q#54, Akien 2026-11-05)

open_questions.text: Which devices besides the librarian hold tables? Today six components use the client. Draft: only the librarian (trees) and the transient tree's owner, if the transient tree is rows.
